title: Improve quantized kernels (INT8/FP8) with smoothquant + dequant-fusion and batching compatibility
author: Rajat Patel
description: Motivation: We observed that quantized inference (INT8 and experimental FP8) performance regresses in common production workloads because the runtime was not emitting fused dequant->matmul kernels and did not apply smoothquant scaling at compile time. This PR introduces a set of compile-time and runtime changes that (1) emit fused dequant+matmul kernels for INT8/FP8 paths, (2) integrate smoothquant scaling into the kernel selection / preparation pipeline, and (3) make the fused kernels compatible with the continuous batching and KV cache code paths so we retain latency SLOs while improving throughput and unit cost. Summary of changes: - Add new fused kernels: runtime/kernels/quant/int8_dequant_fused.cu and runtime/kernels/quant/fp8_dequant_fused.cu with optimized memory layouts and vectorized dequant+GEMM inner loops. - Integrate smoothquant preprocessing into compiler: runtime/compile/smoothquant.rs applies per-channel scaling to weights at build time and records scale tensors for fused kernel consumption. - Kernel selector: runtime/compile/kernel_selector.rs chooses fused kernels when model weights are quantized and smoothquant scales are present, falling back to existing dequant+matmul path when unsupported shapes are detected. - Continuous batching compatibility: runtime/scheduler/batching.rs updated to respect fused kernel alignment constraints (align batch padding and prefix lengths), and batching tests extended to validate tail batching and adaptive padding. - KV cache integration: runtime/kv_cache/cache_manager.rs updated to maintain pinned KV buffers compatible with fused-kernel memory view; added a small fast-path to reuse cached dequant buffers for recurrent requests. - Feature gating and rollout: feature flag enable_quant_fusion off by default; rollout plan described below. Tests and validation: - Microbench harness: tests/quant/bench_int8.py and tests/quant/bench_fp8.py with A100 and RTX8000 profiles. - Unit tests: added kernel-level correctness tests under tests/quant/kernel_tests/*.py and CI GPU smoke test. - End-to-end perf job: cloud-ci/perf/quant_perf_job.yaml that runs comparison suite during nightly perf runs. Results: On internal benchmarks (gpt-like decoder, seq_len=1024, batch=8): - INT8 fused path: median latency -11.8%, p95 latency -9.2%, throughput +24.6% vs previous quant-dequant path on an A100-40GB. - FP8 fused path (experimental): median latency -9.3%, throughput +18% on same workload. - End-to-end cost estimate: ~18-22% reduction in tokens/sec cost for typical production mixes due to reduced op count and better memory locality. Compatibility notes and risks: - Some older CUDA toolkits lack vectorized intrinsics used in fused kernels; the kernel_selector will avoid fused kernels on those environments. - The change is guarded behind enable_quant_fusion and runtime will fall back to the previous path if any kernel mismatch or shape not supported. - KV cache fast-path reuses dequant buffers but keeps ABI-compatible views; this avoids extra allocations in hot loops. Deployment and rollout: - Feature flagged; default off. - Step 1: internal dogfood on Dedicated for 2 days with sampling. - Step 2: opt-in beta for customers with quantized workloads. - Step 3: full enable with gradual region rollout after 2 weeks of stability. Checklist: - [x] Add fused kernels and selector logic - [x] Add smoothquant preprocessing into compile-time flow - [x] Update batcher & KV cache compatibility - [x] Add microbench and unit tests - [x] Nightly perf job - [x] Docs: docs/perf/quantization.md updated to describe runtime flag and expected gains

review_comments: Samantha Ortiz: Nice work, Rajat. Can you add a fallback for older cuBLAS/cuSOLVER versions? The fused kernels assume tensor cores and some intrinsics.
Rajat Patel: Added a runtime check in kernel_selector.rs to avoid fused kernels when CUDA < 11.8 or compute capability < 8.0. Also added the CUDA_compat_check script in CI.
Maya Chen: The batching changes look good, but I'm worried about prefix padding affecting tail latency. Can we add a test that simulates many small prefix lengths?
Rajat Patel: Added tail batching test and updated batching.rs to align padding to 8 elements for fused kernels; results in negligible p50 impact in our tests.
Liam O'Connor: Please ensure experimental FP8 path is clearly gated and does not affect stable metrics. Approving once CI green.
CI: GPU smoke test initially failed on ubuntu-18 nodes due to old driver; Re-run after adding compat check -> PASS.
release_notes: Performance: Emit fused dequant+matmul kernels for INT8 and experimental FP8, integrate smoothquant scaling at compile-time, and improve throughput/latency for quantized workloads. Feature is gated behind enable_quant_fusion. Rollout notes included.
perf_results: INT8 fused: median latency -11.8% p95 -9.2% throughput +24.6% (A100-40GB, seq=1024, batch=8). FP8 experimental: median latency -9.3% throughput +18%. Cost estimate: 18-22% token cost reduction for typical mixes.
testing: Unit tests, kernel-level correctness, microbench harness (A100/RTX8000), nightly perf job. CI GPU smoke test added; CUDA compatibility script ensures safe skip of fused kernels on older drivers.
risk: low; guarded by feature flag and runtime compatibility checks. FP8 path experimental and kept behind explicit enable. KV cache reuse preserves ABI and has safety checks to avoid stale buffers.
